title: Dublin block-fill recede also scales alpha, contradicting the spec/commit/PR-body 'RGB mix, not the alpha twin' mechanism — GPU renders a stronger recede than the verified goldens
evidence:
col := crisis_recede(v, recede, fam)
	col.a = u8(f32(fam.a) * crisis_recede_scale(recede)) — vs spec: "(a) rlsw renders the block's triangle fill OPAQUE — the fill recede rides the RGB mix (crisis_recede), not the alpha twin" and commit 0c86e83: "the fill recede rides the RGB mix (crisis_recede), not the alpha twin"
detail: The alpha scale is inert under rlsw (goldens/palcheck verify RGB-mix only), but the GPU app blends it: family alpha 204→71 compounds the mix, so played-renderer blocks recede far harder than the blessed canon. Docs and code disagree.
recommended_fix: Pick one: drop the alpha line (col.a = fam.a) to match the documented mechanism, or amend spec/PR-body to state the twin applies on GPU and the depth is intentional.

title: Spec Verification claims '7 palcheck FAILs under the factor bypass'; independent re-run at this head measures exactly 6
evidence: "mutation legs RED-then-GREEN (re-run post-fold: 7 palcheck FAILs under the factor bypass)." — re-run evidence: 'palcheck: 6 check(s) FAILED' (both call-site and proc-level bypass variants); §7f calls 'rnd.draw_nodes(&view, &state.topology, &state.crisis, 1100, 1.0)' directly, so its two Dublin legs are factor-immune by design
detail: The load-bearing claim (factor bypass turns palcheck RED) is true and independently reproduced, but the recorded count is wrong (6, not 7; PR body elsewhere says 'five'). Stale cross-round counts could mislead future audits.
recommended_fix: Correct the spec's Verification line to '6 palcheck FAILs under the factor bypass' in the next doc touch; no code change needed.
